P0-A FINDING — TWO PATHWAY AUTHORITIES DISAGREE ABOUT GRP-0422. Evidence, measured at origin 8fcebf5. I am NOT building the fix: the repair needs a field on shared/research/master-offerings/**, which is claude-fable-s7's active lease. Handing it over rather than crossing it.

THE CHAIN, each link verified:

1. The reconciliation KNOWS the hold. config/research/master-catalog-reconciliation-20260821.json carries commerceHolds with exactly one entry, GRP-0422, and applyCatalogReconciliation is wired into the canonical build at scripts/research/build-master-offerings-from-catalog.ts:249.

2. The master-offerings contract HAS NOWHERE TO PUT IT. grep for commerceHold / directOrderHold / hold across shared/research/master-offerings/*.ts returns only two comment mentions — no field. So the hold is known at reconciliation time and has no carrier into the runtime projection.

3. The assisted-order catalog PINS THE HOLD OFF. server/research/assisted-order/production-catalog.ts:154-155 sets `held: false, outOfStock: false` unconditionally, and directEligible is `priced && identity !== null && !providerWorkflowRequired && !classificationPending`.

CONSEQUENCE: GRP-0422 is RUO Research, priced $99, family research_peptides_materials, not provider, not classification-pending. It therefore satisfies directEligible and resolves to direct_order_request THROUGH THE ASSISTED-ORDER DOOR. The `held` rung of decideAssistedOrderAction (action-policy.ts) is unreachable in production because nothing ever sets the flag.

MEANWHILE the EA storefront authority DOES hold it: customer-pathway.ts has commerceHold (your da7985e) and returns assisted_order for it. So the two authorities disagree about the same row. Which one a customer meets depends on which surface drives their order, and that is not a coin I want the launch to flip on a product whose component split we cannot state.

THE SEAM, for whoever you give it to: master-offerings needs to carry the hold from the reconciliation into the projection, production-catalog needs to read it into `held` instead of the literal false, and then action-policy already does the right thing — its availability_review rung is written and tested, just starved of input. My shared/research/launch/peptide-launch-acceptance.test.ts asserts the direct target is 111, so the fix verifies itself when it lands.

WORTH CHECKING SEPARATELY: whether the two pathway authorities should exist at all. customer-pathway.ts and master-offerings/pathway-authority.ts both answer "what can this customer do with this row". One row, two answers, is the same duplicate-authority class the corpus forbids. That is s7's CATALOG-ACTION-UNIFICATION lane, not something I touched.

I have NOT written a failing test for this — it would red the build for everyone. Say the word and I will add one skipped-with-reason, or wire the seam if you would rather delegate it to me than to s7.

Also for s8/general-platform-20: your 29d8e2c may be redundant. I reproduced all three false negatives against the extracted 6291242 blob and confirmed they are real, but the lead ALREADY landed 1b44147 ('Take the safe answer for inline-globstar patterns'), which is in origin and passes all three witness cases. Check 1b44147 before pushing 29d8e2c on top of it.
